**Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin** (née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3)) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.

2011's _Four the Record_ included the singles "Baggage Claim", "Over You", "Fastest Girl in Town", "[Mama's Broken Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart "Mama's Broken Heart")" and "All Kinds of Kinds". Lambert released her fifth album, _Platinum_, in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-ReferenceA-5) The record won the Grammy Award for Best Country Album, and the album's lead single, "Automatic", reached the top five on the Country charts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-6) Her sixth studio album, _The Weight of These Wings_, was released on November 18, 2016, and subsequently certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-RIAA_Certification-7) Her seventh studio album, _Wildcard_, was released on November 1, 2019, and went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Country Album in early 2021. Three singles from the album ("It All Comes Out in the Wash", "Bluebird", "Settling Down") reached the top 20 of the country music charts, and the album's second official single, "Bluebird", became Lambert's first song to top the Billboard Country Airplay Chart as a solo artist since 2012.

She later collaborated with singer-songwriters Jon Randall and Jack Ingram for the album _The Marfa Tapes_, departing from her usual sound and opting for an acoustic, stripped-down feel. It was released on May 7, 2021, to acclaim from critics. Lambert released her eighth solo album, _Palomino_, on April 29, 2022. The same year she was listed on Time 100 by _Time_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-8) Lambert co-wrote and co-produced "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")", a 2025 single by Ella Langley that is the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-9)
Miranda Leigh Lambert was born November 10, 1983,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-dob-1) to Rick and Bev (née Hughes) Lambert in Longview, Texas,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Miranda_Lambert_Biography-2) and was raised in Lindale, Texas. She was named after her great-grandmother, Lucy Miranda.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-usmagazine.com-10) She has one younger brother.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-11)

Her parents met while her mother was attending camp at Southern Methodist University where her father was an on-campus undercover narcotics officer, and they got together a few years later.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12) Her father is a former Dallas police officer who played in a country-rock group called Contraband in the 1970s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-13) Her parents later became private detectives and were hired by lawyers for Paula Jones in the Clinton v. Jones case. After the oil crisis dampened the economy in Texas, her family lost everything.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12)
After the downturn, things got better and her parents began a faith-based ministry and offered their home as a shelter for the victims of domestic violence and their children. Miranda has said that this experience fueled her music and that her song "Gunpowder & Lead" is a reflection of that.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-14)
While still in high school, Lambert made her professional singing debut with "The Texas Pride Band".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-15) She also fronted the house band at the Reo Palm Isle in Longview, Texas,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-16) a long-running venue that had featured Elvis Presley and Willie Nelson, and the place where Brooks & Dunn started out as the house band.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-17)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
The Pistol Annies announced the release of their first Christmas album, _Hell of a Holiday,_ which was released October 22, 2021.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) It contains 10 original songs, a cover of Merle Haggard's "If We Make It Through December", popular Christmas classic "Sleigh Ride", and traditional New Year's song "Auld Lang Syne".[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Price-79) The album was well-received for its original content, and Billboard praised their cover of "If We Make It Through December" as "One of the most striking moments on _Hell of a Holiday"_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-80) They performed many of the songs and discussed the album on December 15's "The Pistol Annies Hell of a Holiday Special", which was made available on Facebook.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-81)
On December 30, 2021, Lambert released "Y'all Means All" in support of the LGBTQ community. The song was used in the trailer for the sixth season of _Queer Eye_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-82) In March 2022 she won Entertainer of the Year at the American Country Music Awards.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-83)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert and Elle King's 2021 collaboration "[Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drunk_(And_I_Don't_Wanna_Go_Home) "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)")" was certified platinum in February, and the two performed the song together at the Ryman Auditorium on Feb 28th to celebrate.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-84) The single has so far reached the top 10 of the country charts.
Lambert released a teaser for a new song titled "Strange" ahead of the ACM Awards, which were held on March 7 in Vegas. She was nominated for 5 awards, marking her record-breaking 16th nomination for Female Vocalist of the Year, and she won Video of the Year for "Drunk (And I Don't Wanna Go Home)", and as well as the top prize of the night, Entertainer of the Year, for the first time in her career.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-85) This brings her tally of total ACM Awards won to 37, the most of all time, and also meant that she is eligible for the ACM's rare and coveted Triple Crown Award.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-86)
On March 10, Lambert released "Strange" alongside a video on her YouTube channel, and announced her eighth solo studio album, _Palomino_, which was released on April 29.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-87) The album includes "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Strange", alongside three re-recorded tracks from her 2021 _Marfa Tapes_ album with Jon Randall and Jack Ingram: "Geraldene", "In His Arms", and "Waxahachie".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-88)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_
Lambert headlined Europe's largest country music festival, C2C: Country 2 Country, from March 11–13, 2022, marking her first performances in the UK/Europe since her headlining tour there in 2017. She performed two songs from _Palomino_ live for the first time ever at her London show on March 11, her single "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Actin' Up".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-89)

### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
[edit]
In March 2023, Lambert announced that she was leaving Sony Music Nashville after nineteen years.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-90)
In April 2024, Lambert announced that she had signed a joint deal with Republic Records and Big Loud, with the latter set to handle country radio promotion and marketing.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-91) She also announced the first single under the new contract, "Wranglers", which was released on May 3, 2024. It serves as the lead single to her tenth studio album, _Postcards from Texas_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-92) Promotional single "Dammit Randy" was released on June 28, 2024, a song she co-wrote with her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-93) The album was released on September 13, 2024.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)
Lambert co-wrote and sang backing vocals on Ella Langley's 2026 No. 1 Billboard 100 hit, "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")." The song's video, set in a Texas bar, features Lambert as a country performer who takes a heartbroken Langley back to Tennessee. Lambert also co-produced Langley's album _Dandelion_ with her and Ben West, co-wrote and features on the track "Butterfly Season", and provides backing vocals on the track "You & Me Time".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-94)

### 2023–present: Label change, _Postcards from Texas_, and _Crisco_
On June 26, 2026, Lambert announced her tenth solo studio album, _Crisco_, would be released on October 2. The project sees Lambert expanding her sound and combining country music with elements of disco, and includes "A Song to Sing", her 2025 duet with Chris Stapleton.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-95)

Title: Miranda Lambert on her new life as a label exec, a landmark 10th album & the power of jokes in songs
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
Miranda Lambert already had a lot of strings to her bow. She is, of course, a record-breaking country artist, with three Grammys, 14 CMA Awards and a host of No.1 albums and singles to her name. She’s also a restaurateur, fashion brand owner, and the founder of dog charity MuttNation Foundation, to name just a few more of her activities.
But this year she’s not only released her 10th album, the brilliant Postcards From Texas, she’s also been making some big moves behind the scenes. For one, the record is her first for Republic Records, having spent her entire career previously on Sony. And that’s not all. Lambert has also teamed up with her fellow artist and collaborator Jon Randall to launch their own record label, Big Loud Texas – an imprint of Big Loud Records. And, as _Music Week_ finds out, she’s taking the whole process of being a label founder very seriously.
Here, we catch up with the country superstar to talk about life as a label executive, and find out more about her latest record…
**So you've teamed up with Jon Randall to launch your own record label. What does that look like in practice for you?**“I'm so excited about it. We're already really in the thick of everything, because we're getting it off the ground. And it's a lot of… It’s a lot! I'm learning so much about the label side versus the artist side the whole time. I'm so happy, I've never really heard of a label hiring or bringing on board artists for the artist. And I just think it's so smart, like there's certain things that only we know, because only we live through it.”

**Could you give an example of that?**“For instance, I got a call – and she doesn't care if I tell this story – from Lainey Wilson. It was some random time of day and she called and said, ‘I just wanted to talk to you because my song just went No.1, it’s my very first one and I just wanted to talk to someone who knew exactly how that felt in the moment.’ Those are the kinds of experiences that only we live through: good, bad and ugly. And so my role as a founder of this label is like, ‘I want to be the artist’s artist’ and make sure that some of the things that I wasn't pleased with on the business side of my career, I can guide another way and also tell them what not to do for the mistakes I made. I don't hold back. I'm not hiding anything. I wish I would have somebody to always call!”
**When it comes to signings, one thing you said you're looking to preserve is the tradition of outlaw country, which is interesting. Country is obviously massive right now, but that outlaw variant isn't often at the forefront anymore…**"I’m absolutely passionate about outlaw country. Think about it, there's probably not a person on this Earth that's not heard of Willie Nelson, you know what I mean? And if they haven't, well, it's time for them to learn! That music, that spirit, was grown in Texas and now it's worldwide, and I want to be part of the next generation of that. At some point [the country sound] divided between Nashville and Texas for some reason. I want to bridge the gap, because country music is country music, and there's so many amazing styles of music in Texas, it's not just country – we have everything. I want to make sure that it is nurtured and that we take care of that for the next generations to come.”
Video 3
**Elsewhere, it feels like it's quite a significant moment for you in your career with Postcards From Texas being your first on Republic, after 20 years at Sony. What appealed about that fresh start?**“I think, as human beings, we understand when something needs to end and when we feel there needs to be a change. I'm so inspired as a songwriter and as an artist in every part of the business right now, I wanted somebody to match that enthusiasm. And Republic did, right off the bat.”

**Anything specific they said or did that made you feel like that?**“Yeah, so many things, besides their track record. [Monte [Lipman]](https://www.musicweek.com/labels/read/umg-launches-universal-arabic-music-headed-by-the-weeknd-s-manager-wassim-sal-slaiby/082976) and Jim Roppo spent, like, three hours with us having old fashions in New York at a bar rooftop, just talking about music. And I was like, ‘Okay, you actually lead with art, this is great.’”
**Free drinks never hurt either…**“Exactly!”
**One of your great lyrical calling cards is your sense of humour, and there’s some great examples of that on Postcards From Texas, but also if you look at Sabrina Carpenter and Chappell Roan, some of the biggest songs this year have also been really funny. What’s the key to writing a humorous lyric that _stay_ funny over the years?**“I appreciate you saying that, and I don't know! But I do know that I think it's so important to have humour, because I'm such a sucker for a sad song so I just feel like there needs to be a balance on a record. So, I like to counterbalance the I Hate Love Songs-style tracks with one like Armadillo. You know, they say ‘recording artist’ for a reason, and it's because you can put on all these hats. It's always been important to me on almost every record to have a song that's kitschy, quippy and shows humour.”

**You've also recorded Dammit Randy with your husband. How did you find that process?**“We haven't done it that much, so it's still new, because he's obviously not a songwriter by trade – he’s a retired police officer, and he's doing some other ventures now. But he's adding songwriter to his resume, and he deserves it. He had some of my favourite lines on the song, and the fact that he's so interested in it gives me inspiration. I see it all through fresh eyes. This is my third record that I've made since I've been married to my husband, and he got to watch me go through three processes, Wild Card, Palomino and now Postcards and he just sees it with such fresh eyes and fire. He’s so interested in the process and such a cheerleader, but also a truth teller. He’s not a yes person, which I love. It's really been fun. I've been doing this a long time, so having him have that enthusiasm where he's kind of in awe of songwriters, i t actually get me more excited. H e's just like, ‘This is crazy, you start off with air, and then you come out with a song four hours later!’ It’s really fun to have that innocence in the room.”

Miranda Lambert’s husband, Brendan McLoughlin, can now add songwriter to his resume.
McLoughlin is credited as a co-writer on Lambert's new song “Dammit Randy” from her 10th studio album, "Postcards from Texas," which was released Sept. 13.
During an interview on TODAY with Hoda & Jenna, Lambert revealed the story behind her husband's role on her album, and she said it all started in 2020 when they had some extra time on their hands.
"We started writing in 2020, when we were home, like for fun, and he was actually pretty good. He's a retired NYPD officer. I was like, 'You're pretty good, actually,'" she recalled. "So then we were writing for this record, and he's dabbled a little bit in it, just with me — for fun."

Miranda Lambert and Brendan McLoughlin at the 2024 MTV Video Music Awards on Sept. 11, 2024, in Elmont, New York.Dimitrios Kambouris / Getty Images
Lambert explained that it helped making music with McLoughlin because he understood everything that she was going through at the time. She said she got out of a long record deal and had "a whole new team" with Republic Records and would also work with Nashville's Big Loud.
"I just felt really excited that I was with a team that led with art," she said. "So I had been, sort of, griping to my husband about the end of that relationship that wasn't serving me anymore. So who better to write a song like that with you than the person that you talk to about it every day? But he was watching football, and I was like, 'You don't get to do both.'"
"And he chose you," Jenna Bush Hager said.
"That's true love," Lambert replied.
Read on to learn more about Miranda Lambert's husband, Brendan McLoughlin.

# Miranda Lambert's husband is a co-writer on her new album. What to know about Brendan McLoughlin
## Brendan McLoughlin is a former police officer
Before McLoughlin met Lambert, he worked as a police officer in New York. The X account of the Midtown South Precinct once shared a photo of McLoughlin in uniform as he posed next to a police dog.
"Officer McLoughlin with Kybo at today’s doggy diving event," the caption read.
However, in 2019, after he got married to Lambert, McLoughlin took a leave of absence from the NYPD, People reported at the time. Then, in 2020, it was revealed that he officially retired from the force.
“His current duty status is retired,” an NYPD DCPI spokesperson told People in a statement.

# Miranda Lambert's husband is a co-writer on her new album. What to know about Brendan McLoughlin
## **Brendan McLoughlin met Miranda Lambert in 2018**
In a 2019 interview with The New York Times, Lambert shared she initially met McLoughlin in 2018 when she was doing press on a morning show to promote her work with her country music group Pistol Annies.
"My husband was doing security there for the show. My girlfriends, the Annies, saw him and knew I might be ready to hang out with someone," she said. "They invited him to our show behind my back. They plucked him for me."
Brendan McLoughlin and Miranda Lambert pictured on April 7, 2019, at the Academy Of Country Music Awards in Las Vegas.John Shearer / Getty Images
"My security guy Tom, he was in on it too. He said to me, 'He’s here. And he’s pretty,'" she laughed.

# Miranda Lambert's husband is a co-writer on her new album. What to know about Brendan McLoughlin
## **Brendan McLoughlin loves to cook**
McLoughlin revealed he loves to make his own meals in a joint interview he did with Lambert at the 2024 MTV VMAs.
When asked what he plans to do on his birthday, McLoughlin told E! News: "I'm probably going to cook, honestly."
He noted that being in the kitchen makes him "happy," and he'll probably strive to make an Italian dish on his birthday.
"That's home for me," he said of loving Italian food.

**Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin** (née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3)) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.

Miranda Lambert already had a lot of strings to her bow. She is, of course, a record-breaking country artist, with three Grammys, 14 CMA Awards and a host of No.1 albums and singles to her name. She’s also a restaurateur, fashion brand owner, and the founder of dog charity MuttNation Foundation, to name just a few more of her activities.
But this year she’s not only released her 10th album, the brilliant Postcards From Texas, she’s also been making some big moves behind the scenes. For one, the record is her first for Republic Records, having spent her entire career previously on Sony. And that’s not all. Lambert has also teamed up with her fellow artist and collaborator Jon Randall to launch their own record label, Big Loud Texas – an imprint of Big Loud Records. And, as _Music Week_ finds out, she’s taking the whole process of being a label founder very seriously.
Here, we catch up with the country superstar to talk about life as a label executive, and find out more about her latest record…
**So you've teamed up with Jon Randall to launch your own record label. What does that look like in practice for you?**“I'm so excited about it. We're already really in the thick of everything, because we're getting it off the ground. And it's a lot of… It’s a lot! I'm learning so much about the label side versus the artist side the whole time. I'm so happy, I've never really heard of a label hiring or bringing on board artists for the artist. And I just think it's so smart, like there's certain things that only we know, because only we live through it.”
texts.1:
**Could you give an example of that?**“For instance, I got a call – and she doesn't care if I tell this story – from Lainey Wilson. It was some random time of day and she called and said, ‘I just wanted to talk to you because my song just went No.1, it’s my very first one and I just wanted to talk to someone who knew exactly how that felt in the moment.’ Those are the kinds of experiences that only we live through: good, bad and ugly. And so my role as a founder of this label is like, ‘I want to be the artist’s artist’ and make sure that some of the things that I wasn't pleased with on the business side of my career, I can guide another way and also tell them what not to do for the mistakes I made. I don't hold back. I'm not hiding anything. I wish I would have somebody to always call!”
**When it comes to signings, one thing you said you're looking to preserve is the tradition of outlaw country, which is interesting. Country is obviously massive right now, but that outlaw variant isn't often at the forefront anymore…**"I’m absolutely passionate about outlaw country. Think about it, there's probably not a person on this Earth that's not heard of Willie Nelson, you know what I mean? And if they haven't, well, it's time for them to learn! That music, that spirit, was grown in Texas and now it's worldwide, and I want to be part of the next generation of that. At some point [the country sound] divided between Nashville and Texas for some reason. I want to bridge the gap, because country music is country music, and there's so many amazing styles of music in Texas, it's not just country – we have everything. I want to make sure that it is nurtured and that we take care of that for the next generations to come.”

**Elsewhere, it feels like it's quite a significant moment for you in your career with Postcards From Texas being your first on Republic, after 20 years at Sony. What appealed about that fresh start?**“I think, as human beings, we understand when something needs to end and when we feel there needs to be a change. **Miranda Leigh Lambert McLoughlin** (née **Lambert**; formerly **Shelton**; born November 10, 1983[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-3)) is an American country music singer–songwriter. Born in Longview, Texas, she started out in early 2001 when she released her self-titled debut album independently. In 2003, she finished in third place on the television program _Nashville Star_, a singing competition that aired on the USA Network. Outside her solo career, she is a member of the Pistol Annies, a group she formed in 2011 alongside Ashley Monroe and Angaleena Presley. Lambert has been honored by the Grammy Awards, the Academy of Country Music Awards and the Country Music Association Awards. Lambert has been honored with more Academy of Country Music Awards than any artist in history. In 2024, Lambert was awarded the Country Icon Award at the [People's Choice Country Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People's_Choice_Awards#People's_Choice_Country_Awards "People's Choice Awards").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-4)
After signing with Epic Records, she released _Kerosene_ in 2005, her first Epic album and second overall. It was certified Platinum in the United States and produced the singles "Me and Charlie Talking", "Bring Me Down", "Kerosene" and "New Strings". All four singles reached the top 40 on the _Billboard_Hot Country Songs. Her second album, _Crazy Ex-Girlfriend_, was released in early 2007. Three of its singles ("Famous in a Small Town", "Gunpowder & Lead" and "More Like Her") peaked within the top 20 on the country songs chart, with "Gunpowder & Lead" becoming her first top 10 entry in July 2008. Her third album, _Revolution_, was released in September 2009. Two of its songs – "The House That Built Me" and "Heart Like Mine" – topped the Hot Country Songs chart.

2011's _Four the Record_ included the singles "Baggage Claim", "Over You", "Fastest Girl in Town", "[Mama's Broken Heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mama's_Broken_Heart "Mama's Broken Heart")" and "All Kinds of Kinds". Lambert released her fifth album, _Platinum_, in 2014.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-ReferenceA-5) The record won the Grammy Award for Best Country Album, and the album's lead single, "Automatic", reached the top five on the Country charts.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-6) Her sixth studio album, _The Weight of These Wings_, was released on November 18, 2016, and subsequently certified Platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-RIAA_Certification-7) Her seventh studio album, _Wildcard_, was released on November 1, 2019, and went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Country Album in early 2021. Three singles from the album ("It All Comes Out in the Wash", "Bluebird", "Settling Down") reached the top 20 of the country music charts, and the album's second official single, "Bluebird", became Lambert's first song to top the Billboard Country Airplay Chart as a solo artist since 2012.

She later collaborated with singer-songwriters Jon Randall and Jack Ingram for the album _The Marfa Tapes_, departing from her usual sound and opting for an acoustic, stripped-down feel. It was released on May 7, 2021, to acclaim from critics. Lambert released her eighth solo album, _Palomino_, on April 29, 2022. The same year she was listed on Time 100 by _Time_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-8) Lambert co-wrote and co-produced "[Choosin' Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choosin'_Texas "Choosin' Texas")", a 2025 single by Ella Langley that is the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-9)
Miranda Leigh Lambert was born November 10, 1983,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-dob-1) to Rick and Bev (née Hughes) Lambert in Longview, Texas,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-Miranda_Lambert_Biography-2) and was raised in Lindale, Texas. She was named after her great-grandmother, Lucy Miranda.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-usmagazine.com-10) She has one younger brother.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-11)

Her parents met while her mother was attending camp at Southern Methodist University where her father was an on-campus undercover narcotics officer, and they got together a few years later.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12) Her father is a former Dallas police officer who played in a country-rock group called Contraband in the 1970s.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-13) Her parents later became private detectives and were hired by lawyers for Paula Jones in the Clinton v. Jones case. After the oil crisis dampened the economy in Texas, her family lost everything.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:0-12)
After the downturn, things got better and her parents began a faith-based ministry and offered their home as a shelter for the victims of domestic violence and their children. Miranda has said that this experience fueled her music and that her song "Gunpowder & Lead" is a reflection of that.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-14)
While still in high school, Lambert made her professional singing debut with "The Texas Pride Band".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-15) She also fronted the house band at the Reo Palm Isle in Longview, Texas,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-16) a long-running venue that had featured Elvis Presley and Willie Nelson, and the place where Brooks & Dunn started out as the house band.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-17)

On December 30, 2021, Lambert released "Y'all Means All" in support of the LGBTQ community. The song was used in the trailer for the sixth season of _Queer Eye_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-82) In March 2022 she won Entertainer of the Year at the American Country Music Awards.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-83)

### 2021–2022: _The Marfa Tapes_, _Palomino_, and Pistol Annies' _Hell of a Holiday_

On March 10, Lambert released "Strange" alongside a video on her YouTube channel, and announced her eighth solo studio album, _Palomino_, which was released on April 29.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-87) The album includes "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Strange", alongside three re-recorded tracks from her 2021 _Marfa Tapes_ album with Jon Randall and Jack Ingram: "Geraldene", "In His Arms", and "Waxahachie".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-88)

She performed two songs from _Palomino_ live for the first time ever at her London show on March 11, her single "If I Was a Cowboy" and "Actin' Up".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-89)

It serves as the lead single to her tenth studio album, _Postcards from Texas_.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-92) Promotional single "Dammit Randy" was released on June 28, 2024, a song she co-wrote with her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-93) The album was released on September 13, 2024.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miranda_Lambert#cite_note-:1-22)

Miranda Lambert already had a lot of strings to her bow. She is, of course, a record-breaking country artist, with three Grammys, 14 CMA Awards and a host of No.1 albums and singles to her name. She’s also a restaurateur, fashion brand owner, and the founder of dog charity MuttNation Foundation, to name just a few more of her activities.
But this year she’s not only released her 10th album, the brilliant Postcards From Texas, she’s also been making some big moves behind the scenes. For one, the record is her first for Republic Records, having spent her entire career previously on Sony. And that’s not all. Lambert has also teamed up with her fellow artist and collaborator Jon Randall to launch their own record label, Big Loud Texas – an imprint of Big Loud Records. And, as _Music Week_ finds out, she’s taking the whole process of being a label founder very seriously.
Here, we catch up with the country superstar to talk about life as a label executive, and find out more about her latest record…
**So you've teamed up with Jon Randall to launch your own record label. What does that look like in practice for you?**“I'm so excited about it. We're already really in the thick of everything, because we're getting it off the ground. And it's a lot of… It’s a lot! I'm learning so much about the label side versus the artist side the whole time. I'm so happy, I've never really heard of a label hiring or bringing on board artists for the artist. And I just think it's so smart, like there's certain things that only we know, because only we live through it.”

**Could you give an example of that?**“For instance, I got a call – and she doesn't care if I tell this story – from Lainey Wilson. It was some random time of day and she called and said, ‘I just wanted to talk to you because my song just went No.1, it’s my very first one and I just wanted to talk to someone who knew exactly how that felt in the moment.’ Those are the kinds of experiences that only we live through: good, bad and ugly. And so my role as a founder of this label is like, ‘I want to be the artist’s artist’ and make sure that some of the things that I wasn't pleased with on the business side of my career, I can guide another way and also tell them what not to do for the mistakes I made. I don't hold back. I'm not hiding anything. I wish I would have somebody to always call!”
**When it comes to signings, one thing you said you're looking to preserve is the tradition of outlaw country, which is interesting. Country is obviously massive right now, but that outlaw variant isn't often at the forefront anymore…**"I’m absolutely passionate about outlaw country. Think about it, there's probably not a person on this Earth that's not heard of Willie Nelson, you know what I mean? And if they haven't, well, it's time for them to learn! That music, that spirit, was grown in Texas and now it's worldwide, and I want to be part of the next generation of that. At some point [the country sound] divided between Nashville and Texas for some reason. I want to bridge the gap, because country music is country music, and there's so many amazing styles of music in Texas, it's not just country – we have everything. I want to make sure that it is nurtured and that we take care of that for the next generations to come.”

**Elsewhere, it feels like it's quite a significant moment for you in your career with Postcards From Texas being your first on Republic, after 20 years at Sony. What appealed about that fresh start?**“I think, as human beings, we understand when something needs to end and when we feel there needs to be a change. **Anything specific they said or did that made you feel like that?**“Yeah, so many things, besides their track record. And I was like, ‘Okay, you actually lead with art, this is great.’”
**Free drinks never hurt either…**“Exactly!”
**One of your great lyrical calling cards is your sense of humour, and there’s some great examples of that on Postcards From Texas, but also if you look at Sabrina Carpenter and Chappell Roan, some of the biggest songs this year have also been really funny. What’s the key to writing a humorous lyric that _stay_ funny over the years?**“I appreciate you saying that, and I don't know! I've been doing this a long time, so having him have that enthusiasm where he's kind of in awe of songwriters, i t actually get me more excited. Miranda Lambert's new album was a family affair.
The country music icon released her ninth major-label album, _Postcards from Texas_, on Friday, Sept. 13, and there's a special collaborator listed in the credits: her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.
Lambert, 40, and McLoughlin, 32, co-wrote her new song "Dammit Randy" with her frequent collaborator Jon Randall.
The performer first did some casual writing with McLoughlin —a retired NYPD officer — during the Covid-19 pandemic lockdown, she tells PEOPLE: "We were writing songs and baking cookies and just keeping ourselves busy, but he was pretty good."
Then as she began to focus on working on _Postcards from Texas_, "Jon Randall picked up a guitar. When that happens, Jon and I usually write a song," Lambert says. "and Brendan was in the room and he kept popping in. I was like, 'All right. If you're going to do this, you got to turn that football game off, and we're going to do it.' He did, and he's done a couple of other co-writes with me."

He ended up with five writing credits on _Crisco_…sounds like he’s a natural.
Last Friday, **Miranda Lambert**released her new disco-inspired album _Crisco_, which she co-produced with Jesse Frasure. It features 12 tracks as Miranda explores “heartbreak and hope, highways and honky-tonks, rhinestones and reflection, creating a record that feels both timeless and refreshingly alive.”
And there’s one writer in particular you might recognize… Miranda’s husband, Brendan McLoughlin.
Brendan is a former NYPD officer, and they met in November of 2018 on the set of Good Morning America while Miranda was performing with her band the Pistol Annies. They secretly married on January 26th, 2019, and it sounds like Brendan has become quite the little writer.
He is listed as a co-writer on five songs on Crisco including the Ella Langley duet **“Snakeskin Boots,”** as well as “Cowgirl Curtsy”, “Two Things Can Be True,” “Till the Going’s Gone” and “Right Where We Left It.”
Interview with Kelleigh Bannen, Miranda says he first started writing with her during COVID, and while he is a huge music fan, he didn’t know about the ins and outs of the business until he met her. Brendan’s first cut was on a song called “Dammit Randy” from Miranda’s _Postcards From Texas_ album:
_**“Music is new to him, this side of it. He loves music, but was thrown into the industry when we met. He’s watching all the moving parts, and we wrote a few songs during COVID, and he was pretty good, honestly. I was like, not bad, not bad…**_
_**I was like, oh no. Like, not for real. He’s not over there on Music Row writing right now, but he was like, oh that’s’ fun, there wasn’t something in the world this morning and now there’s something in the world… he started coming to the studio with me, just because he loves the process.**_
_**We wrote a song called ‘Dammit Randy,’ because he was actually living with me through this complicated time the song was about with this person. He was like, ‘I can speak to this. I’m the one hearing it every night.'”**_

Time went on, and Miranda eventually started writing for Crisco, and when she realized she wanted to make an album, she only had five songs…
Cut to Brendan “talking s***” to Miranda and Jesse one day about how easy songwriting is, and they challenged him to come do a real, professional write with them. They set up a meeting, had a track ready, and Miranda said Brendan got a little nervous when he realized it was pretty serious.
Miranda did admit that he was “pretty good,” and I’d say that he is considering he got five songs on the album:
_**“Jesse Fraser actually, Brendan was talking s*** one day, and he was like, ‘Songwriting’s not hard.’ I was like, ‘Oh, you wanna go?’ I know you’re all fit and stuff, but I want it worse. And Jesse was like, ‘No, so we’re gonna book a write.’ So Jesse and I were writing, and we were like, Brendan, you have to be here at three.**_
_**Jesse had a track pulled up, he comes in his golf clothes and he sits down, and he’s kind of panicking. And we’re like, no this is serious now. Which, he did pretty good. We got a good one, and we were both kind of looking at each other like, why is that okay? Why is that pretty good? But he changed his tune after that.**_
_**He was like, ‘This is hard.’ But he needed to do it. But anyway, we were going to write for ‘Crisco,’ and we only had five songs. And I was like, let’s make a record. Jesse’s like, we only have five songs. I was like, well, gotta get on it then.”**_
Miranda had a few weeks worth of shows in California, so she had her co-writers fly out, and Brendan ended up sitting in on the session:
_**“I was on the west coast for like three weeks because I had shows in California with down time. I was like, why don’t y’all fly out here, Natalie flew out and Jesse, let’s rent a house, let’s finish this… we had some starts, and whatever, and Brendan was there, and it wasn’t discussed, he was just there because he was out on the road with me.**_

_**We start writing, and he’s just sitting there with his little pencil out. I was like, are we gonna do this? And he was like ‘Well, do y’all care if I just sit here?’ They were like, no, we don’t care, because they love him… he said so many great lines. Showing up, and all of us were surprised.**_
_**And then we had to go back and talk about the admin, because he doesn’t really have all that set up, he’s not a songwriter for a living… it was fun, too, it gave me a new energy to watch somebody get so excited about when the line landed, whoever said it.”**_
Some of the songs Brendan helped write are my favorites on the album, and while he has no musical background whatsoever, it sounds like he certainly has a natural way with words.
Of course, he was working with some of the best in the business, but still, that’s impressive, and Miranda spoke about how many good lines he came up with that made the songs a lot better. I guess it’s just the family business now.
There’s no doubt he’s proud of it as he shared on Instagram:
_**“So proud and excited for the release of Crisco. It was an honor to be able to be part of such an incredible album.**_
_**Thank you Miranda Lambert, Telemitry, and Natalie Hemby for allowing me to crash your write in Napa and contributing to five amazing songs, including my first ever radio single.**_
_**Telemitry and Miranda Lambert, watching you both produce this and seeing the joy in the studio between y’all was so special to watch and the perfect match.**_
_**A big thank you to all who took part in this record and MCA for spearheading the release of this album.”**_

Cut to Brendan “talking s***” to Miranda and Jesse one day about how easy songwriting is, and they challenged him to come do a real, professional write with them. They set up a meeting, had a track ready, and Miranda said Brendan got a little nervous when he realized it was pretty serious.
Miranda did admit that he was “pretty good,” and I’d say that he is considering he got five songs on the album:
_**“Jesse Fraser actually, Brendan was talking s*** one day, and he was like, ‘Songwriting’s not hard.’ I was like, ‘Oh, you wanna go?’ I know you’re all fit and stuff, but I want it worse. And Jesse was like, ‘No, so we’re gonna book a write.’ So Jesse and I were writing, and we were like, Brendan, you have to be here at three.**_
_**Jesse had a track pulled up, he comes in his golf clothes and he sits down, and he’s kind of panicking. And we’re like, no this is serious now. Which, he did pretty good. We got a good one, and we were both kind of looking at each other like, why is that okay? Why is that pretty good? But he changed his tune after that.**_
_**He was like, ‘This is hard.’ But he needed to do it. But anyway, we were going to write for ‘Crisco,’ and we only had five songs. And I was like, let’s make a record. Jesse’s like, we only have five songs. I was like, well, gotta get on it then.”**_
Miranda had a few weeks worth of shows in California, so she had her co-writers fly out, and Brendan ended up sitting in on the session:
_**“I was on the west coast for like three weeks because I had shows in California with down time. I was like, why don’t y’all fly out here, Natalie flew out and Jesse, let’s rent a house, let’s finish this… we had some starts, and whatever, and Brendan was there, and it wasn’t discussed, he was just there because he was out on the road with me.**_
texts.2:
_**We start writing, and he’s just sitting there with his little pencil out. I was like, are we gonna do this? And he was like ‘Well, do y’all care if I just sit here?’ They were like, no, we don’t care, because they love him… he said so many great lines. Showing up, and all of us were surprised.**_
_**And then we had to go back and talk about the admin, because he doesn’t really have all that set up, he’s not a songwriter for a living… it was fun, too, it gave me a new energy to watch somebody get so excited about when the line landed, whoever said it.”**_
Some of the songs Brendan helped write are my favorites on the album, and while he has no musical background whatsoever, it sounds like he certainly has a natural way with words.
Of course, he was working with some of the best in the business, but still, that’s impressive, and Miranda spoke about how many good lines he came up with that made the songs a lot better. I guess it’s just the family business now.
There’s no doubt he’s proud of it as he shared on Instagram:
_**“So proud and excited for the release of Crisco. It was an honor to be able to be part of such an incredible album.**_
_**Thank you Miranda Lambert, Telemitry, and Natalie Hemby for allowing me to crash your write in Napa and contributing to five amazing songs, including my first ever radio single.**_
_**Telemitry and Miranda Lambert, watching you both produce this and seeing the joy in the studio between y’all was so special to watch and the perfect match.**_
_**A big thank you to all who took part in this record and MCA for spearheading the release of this album.”**_

*   **Miranda Lambert released her ninth major-label studio album, _Postcards from Texas_, on Friday, Sept. 13**

Miranda Lambert's new album was a family affair.
The country music icon released her ninth major-label album, _Postcards from Texas_, on Friday, Sept. 13, and there's a special collaborator listed in the credits: her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.
Lambert, 40, and McLoughlin, 32, co-wrote her new song "Dammit Randy" with her frequent collaborator Jon Randall.
The performer first did some casual writing with McLoughlin —a retired NYPD officer — during the Covid-19 pandemic lockdown, she tells PEOPLE: "We were writing songs and baking cookies and just keeping ourselves busy, but he was pretty good."
Then as she began to focus on working on _Postcards from Texas_, "Jon Randall picked up a guitar. When that happens, Jon and I usually write a song," Lambert says. "and Brendan was in the room and he kept popping in. I was like, 'All right. If you're going to do this, you got to turn that football game off, and we're going to do it.' He did, and he's done a couple of other co-writes with me."

"Dammit Randy" is the first of their collaborations that she's released, and it came together organically.
"When you're writing about something that you've been talking about and that you've been going through in your life, no one better to have insight on that than your partner at home," Lambert says. "They're living it with you. So, it was the perfect song for him to collaborate on."
As for whether McLoughlin has his own Nashville career in the cards, "The true test is if I'm not in the room," Lambert says, quipping: "So, we'll see what happens if he goes out on his own. We'll see. I'm on the edge of my seat!" More seriously, she adds, "It's fun. He's really proud of it, and I'm really proud of him."

Lambert says watching McLoughlin learn about songwriting brought her back to basics.
"It made me remember that it isn't easy; it's not as easy as it looks. It's putting your heart out there and being vulnerable," the "Alimony" singer says of her husband, whom she wed in 2019. "I think watching him learn like, 'Oh yeah. This is vulnerable. I'm saying my thoughts in this room.' People can laugh all day and say no dumb ideas, but that's not true. You know what I mean? Sometimes you say something, you're like, 'Ooh, that wasn't very good. I shouldn't have said that.' I think watching him learn to be vulnerable was really cool."
Lambert also revisited her Texas roots by returning to her home state to record her first album there in 22 years.
"It's full-circle to me," she says. "It feels like going home to launch this new chapter."

Miranda Lambert's new album was a family affair.
The country music icon released her ninth major-label album, _Postcards from Texas_, on Friday, Sept. 13, and there's a special collaborator listed in the credits: her husband, Brendan McLoughlin.
Lambert, 40, and McLoughlin, 32, co-wrote her new song "Dammit Randy" with her frequent collaborator Jon Randall.
The performer first did some casual writing with McLoughlin —a retired NYPD officer — during the Covid-19 pandemic lockdown, she tells PEOPLE: "We were writing songs and baking cookies and just keeping ourselves busy, but he was pretty good."
Then as she began to focus on working on _Postcards from Texas_, "Jon Randall picked up a guitar. When that happens, Jon and I usually write a song," Lambert says. "and Brendan was in the room and he kept popping in. I was like, 'All right. If you're going to do this, you got to turn that football game off, and we're going to do it.'
